insights.claim: OVMS ships two serving runtime definitions with different scopes: a ClusterServingRuntime for broad cluster access and a namespace-scoped ServingRuntime with RHOAI dashboard integration and GPU support.
insights.reasoning: The ClusterServingRuntime uses a placeholder image tag (openvino/model_server:replace) indicating operator-managed image injection, while the namespace-scoped runtime targets GPU workloads with a latest-gpu tag and different port assignments. This dual-scope pattern allows platform operators to provide a baseline cluster runtime while letting namespace administrators deploy GPU-enabled variants.

insights.claim: OVMS core server has no built-in authentication or authorization mechanism; security is architecturally delegated to the deployment platform or an optional nginx mTLS sidecar.
insights.reasoning: The serving runtime definitions expose HTTP and gRPC ports without any auth configuration. The optional nginx-mtls-auth sidecar in extras/ demonstrates that mTLS is an add-on deployment pattern rather than a core capability. In RHOAI deployments, KServe and Istio service mesh would typically provide the transport security layer.

insights.claim: The OVMS C++ binary links against system OpenSSL from UBI 9 but has no explicit FIPS mode configuration at either build or runtime level.
insights.reasoning: The build installs openssl-devel and the runtime copies the system CA bundle, but neither the build arguments nor the entrypoint configure OpenSSL FIPS mode. FIPS compliance depends entirely on the host system's OpenSSL FIPS provider being active, which is not validated by the application. The nginx sidecar also does not enable FIPS mode explicitly.
